literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 十二项研究符合纳入标准。温度和湿度是最确定的环境决定因素。贝叶斯分层模型是处理空间和时间依赖性的领先分析框架。环境因素和地区社会经济条件之间的相互作用显着影响当地感染风险。总体而言,研究结果表明,这些关系通常是非线性的,并且因地点而异,经常报告阈值效应和地理异质性。 [10.1016/j.puhe.2026.106491]
在体内,MMP-7缺陷型小鼠在RSV攻击后表现出较高的RSV感染、加剧的气道炎症和粘液产生增加。 [10.64898/2026.09.02.748627]
RSVA 显示出最强的时间扩展,并产生以细胞内运输、定位和细胞器组织为中心的晚期反应。RSVB 仍然是最受限制的反应,从早期炎症和信号相关活动转变为后来的干扰素刺激谱。 [10.3389/fgene.2026.1879778]

3195名居民中,发生了526起疑似急性呼吸道感染事件。估计疑似 ARI 风险为 10.2%(95% 可信区间,1.7-43.8)。在 291 次发作中鉴定出病毒:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2(SARS-CoV-2;29.0%)、甲型流感病毒(23.6%)、鼻病毒/肠道病毒(18.8%)、呼吸道合胞病毒(11.8%)、人类偏肺病毒(hMPV;6.4%)、副流感病毒(5.1%)和人类冠状病毒(5.4%)。 [10.1016/j.jamda.2026.106435]

在符合验证标准的 基因组 中,RSV-A 的测序深度(中位数 53,433×;平均值 51,076×)略高于 RSV-B(中位数 49,699×;平均值 46,945×),而 RSV-A 的基因组覆盖度(中位数 97.5%;平均值 96.6%)略低于 RSV-B(中位数 98.3%;平均值 96.6%)。平均 97.6%)。分别使用 16 和 53-57 基因组 评估的运行内和运行间精度显示,基因组 一致性接近 100%,存在 0-5 个核苷酸差异。对 31 个非 RSV 样本的特异性测试未产生假阳性检测。 [10.1128/jcm.00468-26]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Temperature and humidity were the most identified environmental determinants. Bayesian hierarchical models were the leading analytical framework for handling spatial and temporal dependencies. [10.1016/j.puhe.2026.106491]
In vivo, MMP-7-deficient mice displayed higher RSV infection, exacerbated airway inflammation and increased mucus production following RSV challenge. [10.64898/2026.09.02.748627]

RSVA showed the strongest temporal expansion and developed a late response centered on intracellular transport, localization, and organelle organization. RSVB remained the most restricted response, shifting from early inflammatory and signaling-associated activity to a later interferon-stimulated profile. [10.3389/fgene.2026.1879778]
Among 3195 residents, 526 suspected ARI episodes occurred. The estimated suspected ARI risk was 10.2% (95% credible interval, 1.7-43.8). [10.1016/j.jamda.2026.106435]

Among genomes meeting validation criteria, sequencing depth was slightly higher for RSV-A (median 53,433×; mean 51,076×) than RSV-B (median 49,699×; mean 46,945×), whereas genomic coverage was slightly lower for RSV-A (median 97.5%; mean 96.6%) than RSV-B (median 98.3%; mean 97.6%). [10.1128/jcm.00468-26]

papers.title: Clesrovimab, a monoclonal antibody for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus disease in infants: a drug profile.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in young children. In children < 5 years old, it causes an estimated 33 million LRTI episodes and over 100,000 deaths annually, two-thirds of which occur in infants. The licensure of new long-acting monoclonal antibodies and a maternal RSV vaccine offer opportunities for reducing RSV related infant morbidity and mortality. AREAS COVERED: This drug profile reviews clesrovimab (Enflonsia, Merck & Co. Rahway, NJ U.S.A.), an extended half-life human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody, targeting the highly conserved antigenic site IV of the RSV fusion protein. We synthesize evidence from phase 1 to phase 3 clinical trials, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data, regulatory approvals and resistance profiling, drawing on peer-reviewed literature and regulatory sources available until May 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Clesrovimab offers a single, fixed-dose, weight-independent injection per RSV season, with demonstrated safety and efficacy against medically attended RSV disease and hospitalization in infants. Its epitope target is distinct from that of nirsevimab (site Ø) and no cross resistance between the two antibodies has been observed in vitro. Equitable global access to monoclonal antibodies, particularly for low- and middle-income countries, remains critical to reduce the global RSV burden.

papers.title_zh: Clesrovimab,一种用于预防婴儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 病的单克隆抗体:药物概况。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in young children. In children < 5 years old, it causes an estimated 33 million LRTI episodes and over 100,000 deaths annually, two-thirds of which occur in infants. The licensure of new long-acting monoclonal antibodies and a maternal RSV vaccine offer opportunities for reducing RSV related infant morbidity and mortality. AREAS COVERED: This drug profile reviews clesrovimab (Enflonsia, Merck & Co. Rahway, NJ U.S.A.), an extended half-life human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody, targeting the highly conserved antigenic site IV of the RSV fusion protein. We synthesize evidence from phase 1 to phase 3 clinical trials, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data, regulatory approvals and resistance profiling, drawing on peer-reviewed literature and regulatory sources available until May 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Clesrovimab offers a single, fixed-dose, weight-independent injection per RSV season, with demonstrated safety and efficacy against medically attended RSV disease and hospitalization in infants. Its epitope target is distinct from that of nirsevimab (site Ø) and no cross resistance between the two antibodies has been observed in vitro. Equitable global access to monoclonal antibodies, particularly for low- and middle-income countries, remains critical to reduce the global RSV burden.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus in association with environmental factors: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus are the leading causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality globally. Environmental factors influence the spread of these diseases, yet considerable variation remains in how these relationships are modelled across different climates and geographic scales. This systematic review evaluates the use of spatiotemporal frameworks to investigate the relationship between environmental factors and these diseases. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus identified peer-reviewed studies investigating the relationship between environmental factors and influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus using spatiotemporal modelling approaches. Methodological quality was assessed using the Spatial Methodology Appraisal of Research Tool. This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Temperature and humidity were the most identified environmental determinants. Bayesian hierarchical models were the leading analytical framework for handling spatial and temporal dependencies. The interaction between environmental factors and area-level socioeconomic conditions significantly influenced local infection risk. Overall, the findings indicate that these relationships are often nonlinear and vary across locations, with threshold effects and geographical heterogeneity frequently reported. CONCLUSIONS: Spatiotemporal modelling is a valuable tool for investigating the associations between environmental factors and respiratory infection risk. The reviewed evidence suggests that these relationships are often complex, delayed, and, in some cases, nonlinear. This study highlights temperature and humidity as the main environmental factors influencing respiratory infections, noting that local socioeconomic conditions strongly shape their impact. Effective public health surveillance should incorporate localised environmental characteristics and socioeconomic vulnerabilities to better address disease risk across diverse areas.

papers.title_zh: 流感、肺炎和 呼吸道合胞病毒 与环境因素相关的时空分析:系统评价。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus are the leading causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality globally. Environmental factors influence the spread of these diseases, yet considerable variation remains in how these relationships are modelled across different climates and geographic scales. This systematic review evaluates the use of spatiotemporal frameworks to investigate the relationship between environmental factors and these diseases. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus identified peer-reviewed studies investigating the relationship between environmental factors and influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus using spatiotemporal modelling approaches. Methodological quality was assessed using the Spatial Methodology Appraisal of Research Tool. This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Temperature and humidity were the most identified environmental determinants. Bayesian hierarchical models were the leading analytical framework for handling spatial and temporal dependencies. The interaction between environmental factors and area-level socioeconomic conditions significantly influenced local infection risk. Overall, the findings indicate that these relationships are often nonlinear and vary across locations, with threshold effects and geographical heterogeneity frequently reported. CONCLUSIONS: Spatiotemporal modelling is a valuable tool for investigating the associations between environmental factors and respiratory infection risk. The reviewed evidence suggests that these relationships are often complex, delayed, and, in some cases, nonlinear. This study highlights temperature and humidity as the main environmental factors influencing respiratory infections, noting that local socioeconomic conditions strongly shape their impact. Effective public health surveillance should incorporate localised environmental characteristics and socioeconomic vulnerabilities to better address disease risk across diverse areas.

papers.title: The epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalized children in Europe before the widespread implementation of new RSV prophylactic strategies: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to estimate the in-hospital positivity among children in Europe post-COVID-19 and prior to the implementation of the recent RSV prophylactic strategies. A systematic search was conducted across three databases: PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science from 01/01/2021-31/12/2025. Studies enrolling children aged 0-18 years who were hospitalized with respiratory infection and detected positive for RSV were eligible for inclusion. A random-effect model was applied and heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 statistics. Thirty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria, encompasing 66,065 children. The overall pooled RSV in-hospital positivity was 48% (95%CI: 41%-56%). Positivity estimates per year were: 53% (95%CI:49%-56%) for 2021-2022, 49% (95%CI:36%-62%) for 2022-2023, and 62% (95%CI:51%-73%) for 2023-2024 (p = 0.308). RSV positivity in studies with infants (<12-months-old) was 69% vs 30% in studies including older children (0-18 years). Among RSV-positive patients, co-infections were detected in 17%, respiratory support was required in 62% and ICU/NICU admission in 11%. RSV-B predominated over RSV-A during the study period. A substantial burden of RSV-related hospitalizations was detected, especially in infants < 12-months-old; however, the overall pooled positivity estimate should be interpreted with caution. These findings provide an important pre-immunization baseline for evaluating the impact of maternal RSV vaccination and monoclonal antibodies and support the need for continued RSV surveillance across Europe.

A substantial burden of RSV-related hospitalizations was detected, especially in infants < 12-months-old; however, the overall pooled positivity estimate should be interpreted with caution. These findings provide an important pre-immunization baseline for evaluating the impact of maternal RSV vaccination and monoclonal antibodies and support the need for continued RSV surveillance across Europe.

papers.title: Nirsevimab for respiratory syncytial virus prevention: A comprehensive product review.
papers.abstract: Infant RSV prevention is undergoing a public-health paradigm shift toward scalable, broad-eligibility passive immunization. This review examines nirsevimab (Beyfortus®), a long-acting recombinant IgG1κ monoclonal antibody targeting the conserved site Ø of prefusion RSV F protein. Its extended half-life enables season-long protection with a single dose, overcoming key limitations of palivizumab. A validated manufacturing platform and stringent release specifications ensure consistent quality and potency. Pivotal trials demonstrated high efficacy against RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection hospitalization (RSVH), while the pragmatic HARMONIE trial confirmed an 83.2% reduction in RSVH under routine conditions. Postlicensure studies across multiple countries report 70-90% effectiveness against RSVH and substantial reductions in intensive care admissions. Comparative 2024-2025 data further suggest greater protection than maternal RSVpreF vaccination. Nirsevimab represents a scalable public-health intervention that can be used alone or complement maternal RSV vaccination, warranting continued surveillance of effectiveness, safety, and viral escape.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention, specifically examining nirsevimab as a potential intervention for reducing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection hospitalization (RSVH) in infants. The central question is whether nirsevimab can serve as an effective and scalable passive immunization strategy for RSV prevention.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive product review of nirsevimab, a long-acting recombinant IgG1κ monoclonal antibody targeting the conserved site Ø of the prefusion RSV F protein. It includes pivotal trials and a pragmatic HARMONIE trial, which were used to assess efficacy and effectiveness under routine conditions. The review does not explicitly describe the meta-analysis or consensus process, but it relies on these trials for its findings.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Pivotal trials demonstrated high efficacy against RSVH, and the pragmatic HARMONIE trial confirmed an 83.2% reduction in RSVH under routine conditions. Postlicensure studies across multiple countries report 70-90% effectiveness against RSVH and substantial reductions in intensive care admissions. These findings suggest that nirsevimab is a promising intervention for RSV prevention.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that comparative 2024-2025 data suggest greater protection than maternal RSVpreF vaccination, but it does not elaborate on the specific reasons for this discrepancy. Additionally, the review highlights the need for continued surveillance of effectiveness, safety, and viral escape, indicating unresolved questions about long-term outcomes and potential resistance.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Nirsevimab represents a scalable public-health intervention that can be used alone or in combination with maternal RSV vaccination. The review suggests that further research is needed to monitor its effectiveness, safety, and potential for viral escape, as well as to explore its use in different populations and regions.

papers.title_zh: 尼塞韦单抗 用于 呼吸道合胞病毒 预防:全面的产品审查。
papers.source_body_en: Infant RSV prevention is undergoing a public-health paradigm shift toward scalable, broad-eligibility passive immunization. This review examines nirsevimab (Beyfortus®), a long-acting recombinant IgG1κ monoclonal antibody targeting the conserved site Ø of prefusion RSV F protein. Its extended half-life enables season-long protection with a single dose, overcoming key limitations of palivizumab. A validated manufacturing platform and stringent release specifications ensure consistent quality and potency. Pivotal trials demonstrated high efficacy against RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection hospitalization (RSVH), while the pragmatic HARMONIE trial confirmed an 83.2% reduction in RSVH under routine conditions. Postlicensure studies across multiple countries report 70-90% effectiveness against RSVH and substantial reductions in intensive care admissions. Comparative 2024-2025 data further suggest greater protection than maternal RSVpreF vaccination. Nirsevimab represents a scalable public-health intervention that can be used alone or complement maternal RSV vaccination, warranting continued surveillance of effectiveness, safety, and viral escape.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of an ARTIC-based amplicon sequencing assay for whole-genome characterization of respiratory syncytial virus.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a ~15.2 kb negative-sense RNA virus, causes acute respiratory infections in infants and older adults. Its two subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, evolve rapidly, making ongoing monitoring of circulating strains essential. The Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) developed and evaluated an amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing (WGS) assay for RSV surveillance. A total of 214 de-identified remnant clinical specimens (102 RSV-A and 112 RSV-B) with RT-PCR C q values <31 were included. RSV genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom primer sets, with the ARTIC set showing superior performance. Libraries were prepared using a modified Illumina COVIDSeq protocol, sequenced on NextSeq 1000/2000 instruments, and analyzed using the GPHL-RSV-PIPE bioinformatics pipeline. Among genomes meeting validation criteria, sequencing depth was slightly higher for RSV-A (median 53,433×; mean 51,076×) than RSV-B (median 49,699×; mean 46,945×), whereas genomic coverage was slightly lower for RSV-A (median 97.5%; mean 96.6%) than RSV-B (median 98.3%; mean 97.6%). Predominant lineages were A.D.3.1 and A.D.5.2 for RSV-A and B.D.E.1 for RSV-B. For RSV-A, the assay showed 92.8% accuracy, 96.2% sensitivity, 87.2% specificity, 92.6% positive predictive value, and 93.2% negative predictive value. Intra- and inter-run precision assessed using 16 and 53-57 genomes, respectively, showed nearly 100% consensus genome identity with 0–5 nucleotide differences. Specificity testing of 31 non-RSV specimens produced no false-positive detections. Limits of detection were 4.4 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-A and 18.6 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-B. These results demonstrate that the ARTIC-based RSV WGS assay enables near real-time surveillance and strengthens data-driven public health responses to future outbreaks. IMPORTANCE RSV, with two major subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, causes acute respiratory infections that can be severe in infants under 6 months and older adults. Current RSV surveillance at the GPHL relies on the Thermo Fisher TaqMan Gene Expression Capillary assay, which detects and subtypes RSV but lacks resolution for lineage classification and identification of emerging variants. To address this critical gap, GPHL developed and evaluated an amplicon-based WGS assay using 214 de-identified RSV clinical specimens. Genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom-primer sets, with ARTIC primers showing superior performance. The assay demonstrated strong sequencing depth, genomic coverage, specificity, repeatability, reproducibility, and low limits of detection. RSV lineages were accurately determined based on genetic variation. These results establish that the ARTIC-based WGS assay enables near real-time genomic surveillance, supporting monitoring of circulating RSV strains and informing data-driven public health responses.

Predominant lineages were A.D.3.1 and A.D.5.2 for RSV-A and B.D.E.1 for RSV-B. For RSV-A, the assay showed 92.8% accuracy, 96.2% sensitivity, 87.2% specificity, 92.6% positive predictive value, and 93.2% negative predictive value. Intra- and inter-run precision assessed using 16 and 53-57 genomes, respectively, showed nearly 100% consensus genome identity with 0–5 nucleotide differences. Specificity testing of 31 non-RSV specimens produced no false-positive detections. Limits of detection were 4.4 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-A and 18.6 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-B. These results demonstrate that the ARTIC-based RSV WGS assay enables near real-time surveillance and strengthens data-driven public health responses to future outbreaks. IMPORTANCE RSV, with two major subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, causes acute respiratory infections that can be severe in infants under 6 months and older adults. Current RSV surveillance at the GPHL relies on the Thermo Fisher TaqMan Gene Expression Capillary assay, which detects and subtypes RSV but lacks resolution for lineage classification and identification of emerging variants. To address this critical gap, GPHL developed and evaluated an amplicon-based WGS assay using 214 de-identified RSV clinical specimens. Genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom-primer sets, with ARTIC primers showing superior performance. The assay demonstrated strong sequencing depth, genomic coverage, specificity, repeatability, reproducibility, and low limits of detection. RSV lineages were accurately determined based on genetic variation. These results establish that the ARTIC-based WGS assay enables near real-time genomic surveillance, supporting monitoring of circulating RSV strains and informing data-driven public health responses.

papers.title: Seroprevalence and Molecular Characterisation of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Infections in Children at a Tertiary Care Centre in Rural Maharashtra, India.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the foremost viral cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRIs) in children under five years of age, yet surveillance data from rural India remain conspicuously scarce. This cross-sectional study simultaneously characterised RSV seroprevalence and active molecular infection in two non-overlapping paediatric cohorts from Karad, Maharashtra, India (September 2021-August 2023). In Cohort 1 (serological study, n = 290; ≥246 required by a prior calculation), RSV-specific immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies were detected in 182 children (62.8%) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA; indirect format with rheumatoid factor pre-absorption), with the highest positivity in the 2-3-year age group. This rate is interpreted as an indicator of high community-level RSV exposure rather than a precise incidence estimate, given the known limitations of single-timepoint IgM testing in previously exposed children. In Cohort 2 (molecular study, n = 283; ≥233 required), RSV-B was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in 7 of 283 (2.47%) symptomatic children presenting with acute respiratory infection (ARI) or severe ARI (SARI); no RSV-A was identified. The low detection rate is consistent with pandemic-era suppression of respiratory virus transmission. All seven RSV-B strains belonged to the GB5 genotype and formed a phylogenetically distinct local sub-cluster within global GB5 (82% bootstrap support), carrying shared amino acid substitutions in glycoprotein G (A74V, I252T, 165del) and fusion protein F (F12I, S190N, S211N, S389P), numbered relative to the GISAID reference sequence EPI_ISL_1653999 (F precursor). Substitutions S190N and S211N map to the apex region of prefusion F at or adjacent to antigenic site Ø-the primary binding epitope for nirsevimab-though their functional impact on neutralisation was not assessed in vitro and requires dedicated experimental evaluation. A novel predicted N-linked glycosylation site at position F180 was identified in one strain (KIMS-102/2022), with potential but unconfirmed implications for local immune evasion. RSV-B illness was predominantly mild. These findings provide the first combined serological and molecular RSV dataset from rural Maharashtra and underscore the need for region-specific surveillance as RSV prophylactics become available in India.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

papers.title: Matrilysin (MMP-7) Restricts RSV Infection and Airway Inflammation through Proteolysis of CCR3 and RSV-G
papers.abstract: Airway epithelium forms a frontline barrier against microbial invasion through mucociliary clearance and the secretion of antimicrobial and immunomodulatory mediators. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), traditionally viewed as tissue-remodelling enzymes, are also implicated in inflammatory processes and are recognized for their capacity to shap host-pathogen interactions. This study investigates the role of MMP-7 (matrilysin) in airway inflammation and the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. In silico analyses predicted that MMP-7 binds CCR3, the receptor for eotaxin-1/CCL11, and that it also engages the region of the RSV G protein that docks onto CCR3, pointing to a shared biochemical mechanism interfering with both chemokine binding and viral attachment. Mechanistically, MMP-7 proteolytically cleaved CCR3, disrupting eotaxin-1/CCL11 binding and reducing eosinophil activation and chemotaxis, whereas CX3CR1 was unaffected. Importantly, biophysical measurements confirmed that MMP-7 binds and cleaves the RSV G protein, consequently restricting RSV entry and replication in airway epithelial cells. In vivo, MMP-7-deficient mice displayed higher RSV infection, exacerbated airway inflammation and increased mucus production following RSV challenge. Collectively, these findings identify MMP-7 as a key epithelial antiviral effector coordinating both antiviral defense and the regulation of pulmonary inflammation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the role of MMP-7 in airway inflammation and the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The research is motivated by the need to understand how airway epithelium defends against microbial invasion through mucociliary clearance and the secretion of antimicrobial and immunomodulatory mediators.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed in vivo experiments using MMP-7-deficient mice to examine the effects of RSV challenge on infection levels, airway inflammation and mucus production. The research was conducted in a laboratory setting with a focus on airway epithelial cells.
analysis.methods: The study used in silico analyses to predict MMP-7 interactions with CCR3 and the RSV G protein, followed by biophysical measurements to confirm these interactions. In vivo experiments involved assessing RSV infection, airway inflammation and mucus production in MMP-7-deficient mice.
analysis.main_results: In vivo, MMP-7-deficient mice displayed higher RSV infection, exacerbated airway inflammation and increased mucus production following RSV challenge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify MMP-7 as a key epithelial antiviral effector that coordinates both antiviral defense and the regulation of pulmonary inflammation through proteolysis of CCR3 and RSV-G.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide insights into the mechanisms of antiviral defense and inflammation regulation in RSV infection, which could inform the development of targeted therapies and interventions for RSV-related respiratory diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in vivo models and in silico predictions, which may not fully capture human biology. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of a single model system and the absence of direct human data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the role of MMP-7 in RSV infection and airway inflammation. It identifies MMP-7 as an antiviral effector that proteolytically cleaves CCR3, disrupting eotaxin-1/CCL11 binding and reducing eosinophil activation. In vivo experiments with MMP-7-deficient mice showed increased RSV infection, inflammation and mucus production. The findings suggest that MMP-7 coordinates antiviral defense and inflammation regulation, offering potential targets for therapeutic interventions. However, the study's reliance on in vivo models and in silico predictions limits the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了 MMP-7 在气道炎症和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染中的作用。这项研究的动机是需要了解气道上皮如何通过粘膜纤毛清除以及抗菌和免疫调节介质的分泌来防御微生物入侵。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用 MMP-7 缺陷小鼠进行体内实验,以检查 RSV 攻击对感染水平、气道炎症和粘液产生的影响。该研究是在实验室环境中进行的,重点关注气道上皮细胞。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用计算机分析来预测 MMP-7 与 CCR3 和 RSV G 蛋白的相互作用,然后通过生物物理测量来确认这些相互作用。体内实验涉及评估 MMP-7 缺陷小鼠的 RSV 感染、气道炎症和粘液产生。
elements_zh.main_results: 在体内,MMP-7缺陷型小鼠在RSV攻击后表现出较高的RSV感染、加剧的气道炎症和粘液产生增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果确定 MMP-7 是关键的上皮 抗病毒药物 效应子,通过 CCR3 和 RSV-G 的蛋白水解来协调 抗病毒药物 防御和肺部炎症调节。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为了解 RSV 感染中 抗病毒药物 防御和炎症调节的机制提供了见解,这可以为 RSV 相关呼吸系统疾病的靶向治疗和干预措施的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对体内模型和计算机预测的依赖而受到限制,这可能无法完全捕捉人类生物学。由于使用单一模型系统并且缺乏直接的人类数据,证据的强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 气道上皮通过黏液纤毛清除作用和分泌抗菌及免疫调节介质,形成抵御微生物入侵的第一道防线。基质金属蛋白酶(MMPs),传统上被视为组织重塑酶,也参与炎症过程,并被认识到其能够影响呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染中气道上皮与病原体的相互作用。本研究探讨了MMP-7(基质金属蛋白酶-7)在气道炎症及呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染中的作用。计算机模拟分析预测MMP-7能够结合CCR3受体(eotaxin-1/CCL11的受体),并且还能结合RSV G蛋白与CCR3结合的区域,提示存在一种共同的生化机制,干扰化学引诱素结合和病毒附着。从机制上看,MMP-7通过蛋白酶活性切割CCR3,从而破坏eotaxin-1/CCL11的结合,减少嗜酸性粒细胞的激活和趋化作用,而CX3CR1则不受影响。重要的是,生物物理测量证实MMP-7能够结合并切割RSV G蛋白,从而限制RSV在气道上皮细胞中的进入和复制。在体内实验中,MMP-7缺失的小鼠在RSV感染后表现出更高的感染水平、更严重的气道炎症和增加的黏液分泌。综上所述,这些发现确定了MMP-7作为关键的气道上皮效应因子,协调气道防御和肺部炎症的调控。

papers.title: Clinical Impact of Acute Respiratory Virus Infections in Nursing Home Residents.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the suspected acute respiratory infection (ARI) risk and the clinical impact of a range of respiratory viruses in Dutch nursing home (NH) residents. DESIGN: Prospective cohort study (March 2023-May 2025). SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Residents from 15 Dutch NHs were enrolled when suspected of an ARI. METHODS: Clinical data were collected on days 0, 14, and 28. Residual nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs were tested for a broad respiratory virus panel. A Bayesian multilevel logistic model including seasonal and NH-level random effects estimated suspected ARI risk. Relative clinical outcomes were compared by virus. RESULTS: Among 3195 residents, 526 suspected ARI episodes occurred. The estimated suspected ARI risk was 10.2% (95% credible interval, 1.7-43.8). Viruses were identified in 291 episodes: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; 29.0%), influenza A virus (23.6%), rhinovirus/enterovirus (18.8%), respiratory syncytial virus (11.8%), human metapneumovirus (hMPV; 6.4%), parainfluenza viruses (5.1%), and human coronaviruses (5.4%). hMPV and respiratory syncytial virus tended to be associated with higher odds of moderate or severe disease, and hMPV was linked to a 4-fold increase in bed hours. Influenza A was associated with delayed recovery, oxygen requirement, and a 3-fold risk of secondary bacterial pneumonia. SARS-CoV-2 cases had higher estimated odds of recovery by day 14 and spent fewer additional hours in bed during ARI episodes. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Influenza remains a major contributor to ARI burden in NH residents, whereas SARS-CoV-2 has relatively limited impact. The pronounced clinical impact of hMPV suggests its relevance for ARI management in this population.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the clinical impact of respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, in Dutch nursing home residents. A prospective cohort study from March 2023 to May 2025 enrolled 3195 residents suspected of an acute respiratory infection (ARI). Clinical data were collected on days 0, 14, and 28, and residual swabs were tested for a broad virus panel. The study found that respiratory syncytial virus was identified in 11.8% of ARI episodes and showed a pronounced clinical impact, suggesting its relevance for ARI management in this population. The results indicate that respiratory syncytial virus contributes significantly to ARI burden, with implications for targeted surveillance and care. The study's observational design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in its findings, but the comprehensive methods and statistical modeling provide strong evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查荷兰疗养院(NH)居民的疑似急性呼吸道感染(ARI)风险以及一系列呼吸道病毒的临床影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究于 2023 年 3 月至 2025 年 5 月进行,招募了来自 15 家荷兰疗养院的疑似 ARI 的居民。
elements_zh.methods: 在第 0、14 和 28 天收集临床数据,并对残留的鼻咽和口咽拭子进行广泛的呼吸道病毒检测。包括季节性和 NH 水平随机效应的贝叶斯多级逻辑模型估计了疑似 ARI 风险。通过病毒比较相对临床结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 3195名居民中,发生了526起疑似急性呼吸道感染事件。估计疑似 ARI 风险为 10.2%(95% 可信区间,1.7-43.8)。在 291 次发作中鉴定出病毒:严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2(SARS-CoV-2;29.0%)、甲型流感病毒(23.6%)、鼻病毒/肠道病毒(18.8%)、呼吸道合胞病毒(11.8%)、人类偏肺病毒(hMPV;6.4%)、副流感病毒(5.1%)和人类冠状病毒(5.4%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 呼吸道合胞病毒 的显着临床影响表明其与该人群 ARI 管理的相关性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了 呼吸道合胞病毒 在疗养院居民 ARI 临床负担中的重要性,为有针对性的 呼吸道合胞病毒 和管理策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到观察设计和潜在混杂因素的限制,但由于全面的呼吸道病毒组和统计模型,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Evaluation of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F IgG Antibodies in Japanese Mother–Infant Pairs Following Maternal Abrysvo Vaccination and in Infants Hospitalized with RSV Infection
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The approval of Abrysvo, a maternal bivalent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F (pre-F) vaccine, marked a major milestone in pediatric prophylaxis. However, real-world serological data on transplacental antibody transfer in Asian populations remains limited. This brief report evaluated serum RSV pre-F immunoglobulin G (IgG) geometric mean titers (GMTs) across three distinct Japanese cohorts. Methods: This single-center, comparative study analyzed neonates born to Abrysvo-vaccinated mothers (n = 12), neonates born to unvaccinated mothers (n = 40), and infants aged <6 months hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection (n = 18) using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results: Neonates of vaccinated mothers exhibited significantly higher pre-F IgG GMTs (4.74; 95% CI: 4.30–5.18) than those of unvaccinated mothers (3.80; 95% CI: 3.50–4.14). Conversely, infants requiring hospitalization for RSV infection demonstrated critically low pre-F IgG GMTs (1.08; 95% CI: 0.65–2.15), revealing statistically significant differences across all three groups (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Maternal immunization with Abrysvo significantly enhances passive humoral immunity in Japanese neonates compared to natural background immunity. Given the severe antibody deficiency observed in hospitalized infants, expanding maternal vaccination coverage is a high-priority public health strategy to mitigate the pediatric RSV burden in the post-pandemic era.

papers.title_zh: 母体 Abrysvo 呼吸道合胞病毒 后日本母婴对以及因 RSV 感染住院的婴儿中 呼吸道合胞病毒 预融合 F IgG 抗体的评估
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: The approval of Abrysvo, a maternal bivalent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F (pre-F) vaccine, marked a major milestone in pediatric prophylaxis. However, real-world serological data on transplacental antibody transfer in Asian populations remains limited. This brief report evaluated serum RSV pre-F immunoglobulin G (IgG) geometric mean titers (GMTs) across three distinct Japanese cohorts. Methods: This single-center, comparative study analyzed neonates born to Abrysvo-vaccinated mothers (n = 12), neonates born to unvaccinated mothers (n = 40), and infants aged <6 months hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection (n = 18) using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results: Neonates of vaccinated mothers exhibited significantly higher pre-F IgG GMTs (4.74; 95% CI: 4.30–5.18) than those of unvaccinated mothers (3.80; 95% CI: 3.50–4.14). Conversely, infants requiring hospitalization for RSV infection demonstrated critically low pre-F IgG GMTs (1.08; 95% CI: 0.65–2.15), revealing statistically significant differences across all three groups (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Maternal immunization with Abrysvo significantly enhances passive humoral immunity in Japanese neonates compared to natural background immunity. Given the severe antibody deficiency observed in hospitalized infants, expanding maternal vaccination coverage is a high-priority public health strategy to mitigate the pediatric RSV burden in the post-pandemic era.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目标:Abrysvo 的批准是一种母体二价 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预输注 F (pre-F) 疫苗,标志着儿科预防的一个重要里程碑。然而,亚洲人群经胎盘抗体转移的真实血清学数据仍然有限。这份简短的报告评估了三种不同的日本 队列研究 的血清 RSV pre-F 免疫球蛋白 G (IgG) 几何平均滴度 (GMT)。方法:这项单中心比较研究使用酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA) 分析了接种 Abrysvo 疫苗的母亲所生的新生儿 (n = 12)、未接种疫苗的母亲所生的新生儿 (n = 40) 以及因实验室确诊的 RSV 感染而住院的 6 个月以下婴儿 (n = 18)。结果:接种疫苗的母亲的新生儿表现出比未接种疫苗的母亲 (3.80;95% CI: 3.50–4.14) 显着更高的前 F IgG GMT (4.74;95% CI: 4.30–5.18)。相反,因 RSV 感染而需要住院治疗的婴儿表现出极低的 pre-F IgG GMT(1.08;95% CI:0.65–2.15),显示所有三组之间存在统计学显着差异(p < 0.001)。结论:与自然背景免疫相比,Abrysvo 母体免疫显着增强了日本新生儿的被动体液免疫。鉴于住院婴儿中观察到的严重抗体缺乏症,扩大孕产妇 疫苗接种 覆盖范围是减轻大流行后时代儿科 RSV 负担的一项高度优先的公共卫生战略。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.title: Detection of nirsevimab-resistant RSV-B variants in children carrying the F:N201T substitution through genomic surveillance, Spain, 2025/26 season
papers.abstract: During Spain's 2025/26 RSV season, three children were infected with RSV-B viruses carrying the F protein N201T substitution. Two who received nirsevimab that season were hospitalised (one required intensive care); the third was treated previously. Recombinant expression studies confirmed reduced nirsevimab recognition. Genomic data indicated sporadic emergence across distinct RSV-B backgrounds rather than expansion of a single lineage. Findings highlight the importance of combining genomic surveillance with antigenic characterisation to detect and interpret variants with reduced susceptibility to antibody-based prevention.

papers.title: Construction and application of a novel respiratory syncytial virus vaccine based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children, immunocompromised adults, and elderly individuals with comorbidities. Its high pathogenicity and associated mortality impose a substantial disease burden on public health. Vaccination represents a key strategy for preventing RSV infection. However, currently approved RSV vaccines exhibit limitations. For instance, Abrysvo and Arexvy pose potential safety risks in clinical use, and the long-term protective efficacy of mRESVIA may wane over time. Therefore, this article proposes and explores a novel RSV vaccine strategy utilizing Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles (Bt OMVs) as a delivery platform. This strategy capitalizes on the unique advantages of Bt OMVs, including efficient mucosal delivery, low inherent toxicity, and targeted modulation of T cell homeostasis—specifically enhancing Treg and Th1 responses while suppressing excessive Th2 and Th17 activation, which serves as the core mechanism for preventing vaccine-enhanced disease (VED)—to effectively present the RSV F protein antigen. It offers a novel approach to develop next-generation RSV vaccines that combine durable protection with enhanced clinical safety.

Its high pathogenicity and associated mortality impose a substantial disease burden on public health. Vaccination represents a key strategy for preventing RSV infection. However, currently approved RSV vaccines exhibit limitations. For instance, Abrysvo and Arexvy pose potential safety risks in clinical use, and the long-term protective efficacy of mRESVIA may wane over time. Therefore, this article proposes and explores a novel RSV vaccine strategy utilizing Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles (Bt OMVs) as a delivery platform. This strategy capitalizes on the unique advantages of Bt OMVs, including efficient mucosal delivery, low inherent toxicity, and targeted modulation of T cell homeostasis—specifically enhancing Treg and Th1 responses while suppressing excessive Th2 and Th17 activation, which serves as the core mechanism for preventing vaccine-enhanced disease (VED)—to effectively present the RSV F protein antigen. It offers a novel approach to develop next-generation RSV vaccines that combine durable protection with enhanced clinical safety.

analysis.summary_en: Respiratory syncytial virus causes severe disease across vulnerable populations, and existing vaccines are limited by safety concerns and waning protection. To address this gap, the authors propose a novel RSV vaccine that employs Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles as a mucosal delivery platform, aiming to enhance T‐cell regulation and avoid vaccine‐enhanced disease. While the concept promises durable protection and improved safety, the provided evidence lacks details on study design, methods, results, and limitations, preventing a full evaluation of efficacy or generalizability. Consequently, the claim remains preliminary, and further experimental data are needed to substantiate the vaccine’s potential impact on RSV prevention.

papers.title: Transcriptional signatures of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection using relaxed magnitude altitude score with hub-centric network analysis (RMAS-HCNA)
papers.abstract: Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus A (RSVA) and respiratory syncytial virus B (RSVB) may induce distinct airway host responses. We compared them with influenza A virus (IAV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in airway organ tissue equivalents (OTEs) and developed the Relaxed Magnitude Altitude Score with Hub-Centric Network Analysis framework (RMAS-HCNA). Methods OTEs were infected with RSVA-GFP5 or RSVB-GFP3 at low multiplicity of infection and profiled at 24 and 72 h using the NanoString nCounter Host Response Panel. Previous IAV and hMPV profiles were integrated. Analyses included source-matched differential expression, cross-virus ranking, network-based module selection, nested cross-validation, and Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment. Results RSVA showed the strongest temporal expansion and developed a late response centered on intracellular transport, localization, and organelle organization. RSVB remained the most restricted response, shifting from early inflammatory and signaling-associated activity to a later interferon-stimulated profile. IAV maintained a broad antiviral response, whereas hMPV combined limited induction with extensive late downregulation of stress, catabolic, metabolic, and transport-related processes. A shared antiviral component was present across infections, while downregulated responses were largely virus dependent. Under five-fold outer and four-fold inner nested cross-validation, the selected genes achieved a mean outer-test Macro F1 of 0.859 and balanced accuracy of 0.888, compared with 0.604 and 0.616 for the all-gene comparator. Discussion The four viruses shared an antiviral foundation but followed distinct temporal and functional trajectories. The framework identified compact, biologically representative panels that generalized better than the complete measured gene set, although independent genome-wide and in vivo validation remains necessary.

We compared them with influenza A virus (IAV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in airway organ tissue equivalents (OTEs) and developed the Relaxed Magnitude Altitude Score with Hub-Centric Network Analysis framework (RMAS-HCNA). Methods OTEs were infected with RSVA-GFP5 or RSVB-GFP3 at low multiplicity of infection and profiled at 24 and 72 h using the NanoString nCounter Host Response Panel. Previous IAV and hMPV profiles were integrated. Analyses included source-matched differential expression, cross-virus ranking, network-based module selection, nested cross-validation, and Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment. Results RSVA showed the strongest temporal expansion and developed a late response centered on intracellular transport, localization, and organelle organization. RSVB remained the most restricted response, shifting from early inflammatory and signaling-associated activity to a later interferon-stimulated profile. IAV maintained a broad antiviral response, whereas hMPV combined limited induction with extensive late downregulation of stress, catabolic, metabolic, and transport-related processes. A shared antiviral component was present across infections, while downregulated responses were largely virus dependent. Under five-fold outer and four-fold inner nested cross-validation, the selected genes achieved a mean outer-test Macro F1 of 0.859 and balanced accuracy of 0.888, compared with 0.604 and 0.616 for the all-gene comparator. Discussion The four viruses shared an antiviral foundation but followed distinct temporal and functional trajectories. The framework identified compact, biologically representative panels that generalized better than the complete measured gene set, although independent genome-wide and in vivo validation remains necessary.

The research compared these viruses with influenza A virus (IAV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in airway organ tissue equivalents (OTEs). papers.abstract_zh: 简介 呼吸道合胞病毒 A (RSVA) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 B (RSVB) 可能会引起不同的气道 宿主 反应。我们将它们与甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 的气道器官组织等效物 (OTE) 进行比较,并使用以枢纽为中心的网络分析框架 (RMAS-HCNA) 开发了松弛幅度高度评分。方法 OTE 以低感染复数感染 RSVA-GFP5 或 RSVB-GFP3,并使用 NanoString nCounter 宿主 响应面板在 24 小时和 72 小时进行分析。集成了以前的 IAV 和 hMPV 配置文件。分析包括源匹配差异表达、交叉病毒排序、基于网络的模块选择、嵌套交叉验证和基因本体生物过程富集。结果 RSVA 显示出最强的时间扩展,并产生以细胞内运输、定位和细胞器组织为中心的晚期反应。RSVB 仍然是最受限制的反应,从早期炎症和信号相关活动转变为后来的干扰素刺激谱。IAV 维持广泛的 抗病毒药物 反应,而 hMPV 将有限的诱导与应激、分解代谢、代谢和运输相关过程的广泛后期下调结合起来。感染过程中存在共同的 抗病毒药物 成分,而下调的反应很大程度上依赖于病毒。在五重外部和四重内部嵌套交叉验证下,所选基因的平均外部测试宏 F1 为 0.859,平衡精度为 0.888,而全基因比较器的平衡精度为 0.604 和 0.616。讨论 这四种病毒共享 抗病毒药物 基础,但遵循不同的时间和功能轨迹。尽管仍然需要独立的 基因组 范围和体内验证,但该框架确定了紧凑的、具有生物学代表性的面板,其概括性优于完整的测量基因集。

papers.title: Concurrent Sigmoid Microperforation in the Setting of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in an Adult Patient: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory pathogen primarily associated with pediatric infections; however, RSV infection is recognized as a significant cause of illness in adults, particularly during winter months.Despite its well-established association with respiratory disease, RSV can also present with extrapulmonary manifestations, including gastrointestinal symptoms.Here, we present the case of a 65-year-old male who presented with dyspnea and abdominal pain and tested positive for RSV.Concurrently, the patient was discovered to have a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis on abdominal imaging.Surgical intervention was deferred due to a high perioperative risk, and the patient was treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics.Shortly after, the patient developed multiple abdominal abscesses, which were treated with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and drain placement.RSV has been documented to cause gastrointestinal pathology in children by weakening the bowel wall.As RSV was identified in this patient in the setting of gastrointestinal pathology, it is hypothesized that RSV may have contributed to this patient's gastrointestinal condition.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory pathogen primarily associated with pediatric infections; however, RSV infection is recognized as a significant cause of illness in adults, particularly during winter months. Despite its well-established association with respiratory disease, RSV can also present with extrapulmonary manifestations, including gastrointestinal symptoms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study is a case report describing a 65-year-old male patient who presented with dyspnea and abdominal pain and tested positive for RSV. The patient was found to have a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis on abdominal imaging.
analysis.methods: The patient was tested for RSV and underwent abdominal imaging to identify gastrointestinal pathology. Surgical intervention was deferred due to a high perioperative risk, and the patient was treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics. Subsequently, the patient developed multiple abdominal abscesses, which were managed with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and drain placement.
analysis.main_results: The patient tested positive for RSV and was found to have a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis on abdominal imaging. He developed multiple abdominal abscesses, which were treated with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and drain placement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: It is hypothesized that RSV may have contributed to the patient's gastrointestinal condition, as RSV has been documented to cause gastrointestinal pathology in children by weakening the bowel wall.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case report highlights the potential for RSV to cause extrapulmonary manifestations, including gastrointestinal complications, in adults, which may inform broader surveillance and diagnostic approaches for RSV-related conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is based on direct clinical observations and documented treatment outcomes, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 65-year-old male patient with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection who also presented with a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis and multiple abdominal abscesses. The patient was treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics and later underwent CT-guided percutaneous drainage for the abscesses. The case suggests that RSV may contribute to gastrointestinal complications in adults, expanding the understanding of its extrapulmonary manifestations. papers.title: Respiratory syncytial virus subtype influences pediatric airway microbiome independent of viral burden
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the main cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. Multiple studies have demonstrated that respiratory microbiome composition is strongly associated with susceptibility to viral infection, disease severity, and subsequent respiratory outcomes. However, it is still unclear how different RSV subtypes affect the respiratory microbiome. Results In this study, we examined the airway microbiome in children infected with RSV-A (n = 18) or RSV-B (n = 12) and compared them with recovered individuals (n = 7) using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing. We found 598 bacterial genera across 39 phyla in 37 samples, with Bacillota , Pseudomonadota , and Actinomycetota being the most common. While overall microbial diversity stayed stable during infection, RSV changed the makeup of the microbial communities, suggesting that infection mainly reorganizes ecological relationships rather than reducing the number of bacterial types. Our analyses showed that the microbiome differed by RSV subtype (PERMANOVA R2 = 0.249, P = 0.016), with RSV-A samples showing more variation than RSV-B. Differential abundance analysis revealed that RSV-A caused greater changes in the microbiome, with 81 affected genera compared to 31 in RSV-B. Viral load did not have a noticeable effect on microbiome structure, as C t values explained only 1.8% of the variation (R2 = 0.018, P = 0.776). Despite these changes, a core group of 45 bacterial genera was found in all groups, including RSV-A, RSV-B, and recovered individuals. Conclusions Our results indicate that RSV subtype is a key factor shaping the respiratory microbiome, more so than viral load, and leads to distinct microbial patterns in the pediatric airway. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized aspect of RSV infection and suggest that differences between subtypes may affect disease progression, immune response, and clinical outcomes.

papers.title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 亚型影响儿童气道微生物组,与病毒负荷无关
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the main cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. Multiple studies have demonstrated that respiratory microbiome composition is strongly associated with susceptibility to viral infection, disease severity, and subsequent respiratory outcomes. However, it is still unclear how different RSV subtypes affect the respiratory microbiome. Results In this study, we examined the airway microbiome in children infected with RSV-A (n = 18) or RSV-B (n = 12) and compared them with recovered individuals (n = 7) using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing. We found 598 bacterial genera across 39 phyla in 37 samples, with Bacillota , Pseudomonadota , and Actinomycetota being the most common. While overall microbial diversity stayed stable during infection, RSV changed the makeup of the microbial communities, suggesting that infection mainly reorganizes ecological relationships rather than reducing the number of bacterial types. Our analyses showed that the microbiome differed by RSV subtype (PERMANOVA R2 = 0.249, P = 0.016), with RSV-A samples showing more variation than RSV-B. Differential abundance analysis revealed that RSV-A caused greater changes in the microbiome, with 81 affected genera compared to 31 in RSV-B. Viral load did not have a noticeable effect on microbiome structure, as C t values explained only 1.8% of the variation (R2 = 0.018, P = 0.776). Despite these changes, a core group of 45 bacterial genera was found in all groups, including RSV-A, RSV-B, and recovered individuals. Conclusions Our results indicate that RSV subtype is a key factor shaping the respiratory microbiome, more so than viral load, and leads to distinct microbial patterns in the pediatric airway. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized aspect of RSV infection and suggest that differences between subtypes may affect disease progression, immune response, and clinical outcomes.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是婴幼儿严重下呼吸道感染的主要原因。多项研究表明,呼吸道微生物组的组成与病毒感染的易感性、疾病的严重程度和随后的呼吸道结果密切相关。然而,目前尚不清楚不同 RSV 亚型如何影响呼吸道微生物组。结果在本研究中,我们检查了感染 RSV-A (n = 18) 或 RSV-B (n = 12) 的儿童的气道微生物组,并使用全长 16S rRNA 基因测序将其与康复个体 (n = 7) 进行比较。我们在 37 个样本中发现了 39 个门的 598 个细菌属,其中杆菌门、假单胞菌门和放线菌门是最常见的。虽然总体微生物多样性在感染期间保持稳定,但 RSV 改变了微生物群落的构成,这表明感染主要是重组生态关系,而不是减少细菌类型的数量。我们的分析表明,微生物组因 RSV 亚型而异(PERMANOVA R2 = 0.249,P = 0.016),RSV-A 样本比 RSV-B 表现出更多变异。差异丰度分析显示,RSV-A 引起微生物组发生更大的变化,受影响的属有 81 个,而 RSV-B 受影响的属有 31 个。病毒载量对微生物组结构没有明显影响,因为 Ct 值仅解释了 1.8% 的变异(R2 = 0.018,P = 0.776)。尽管有这些变化,在所有群体中都发现了 45 个细菌属的核心群体,包括 RSV-A、RSV-B 和康复个体。结论 我们的结果表明,RSV 亚型是影响呼吸道微生物组的关键因素,其作用比病毒载量更重要,并导致儿科气道中独特的微生物模式。这些发现强调了 RSV 感染以前未被认识的一个方面,并表明亚型之间的差异可能会影响疾病进展、免疫应答 和临床结果。

papers.full_text: Abstract Existing reports of RSV disease burden in adults focus primarily on hospitalisation while little is known about RSV disease burden in community and primary-care settings. In this study, we aimed to estimate RSV-associated acute respiratory infection (ARI) disease burden in community and primary-care settings among adults in high-income countries. We conducted a systematic literature review (PROSPERO registration: CRD42022377741) to identify published studies on RSV morbidity and mortality burden in community (including ill adults seeking or not seeking health care identified by prospective cohort studies with active case ascertainment) or primary-care settings (including outpatient and emergency department, ED) in adults in high-income countries. We accounted for the potential case under-ascertainment of RSV related to the imperfect test sensitivity of respiratory specimens and diagnostic tests by applying correction factors to the reported incidence rate and positive proportion estimates in individual studies. We estimated incidence rate and RSV positive proportion among those tested with acute respiratory illness by age group and setting. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to synthesise the estimates across studies. A total of six studies contributed to RSV incidence rate estimates in community or primary-care settings. The adjusted RSV incidence rate in the community was similar between persons aged 18–49 years (6104/100,000 person-years, 95% CI: 3737–9971; 1 study) and ≥ 50 years (5311/100,000 person-years, 95% CI: 3690–7643; 2 studies). In the outpatient setting, the adjusted RSV incidence rate increased with age, ranging from 2231/100,000 person-years (95% CI: 1088–4577; 2 studies) in adults aged 18–49 years to 4079/100,000 person-years (95% CI: 2759–6031; 3 studies) person-years in adults aged ≥ 65 years. Based on 1 study, RSV incidence rate in the ED was comparable between those aged 18–49 years (309/100,000, 142–676) and 50–64 years (300/100,000, 98–919), and was higher in adults aged ≥65 years (685/100,000 person-years, 95% CI: 258–2058). Based on five studies, the adjusted RSV positive proportion in adults with ARI was generally similar across the community, outpatient, and ED settings (range: 3.7–5.1%). This study revealed substantial RSV disease burden in community and primary-care settings across all age strata of adults in high-income countries. Compared to adults under age 65 years, older adults have higher RSV incidence rates in the ED and slightly higher incidence rates in the outpatient setting. These findings highlight the importance of considering RSV disease burden in community and primary-care settings when anticipating the potential impact of RSV vaccination. papers.title: Etiology and Clinical Manifestations of Acute Respiratory Infections in Pediatric Patients: A Retrospective Study in Moscow, Russia
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute respiratory viral infections (ARVIs) are the leading cause of pediatric morbidity and exhibit considerable clinical heterogeneity. The analysis of clinical and etiological associations, as well as the identification of factors linked to severe ARVI cases, is essential for effective epidemiological surveillance. Methods: A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted including 1362 non-COVID-19 pediatric cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs), registered between 2021 and 2024. Viral pathogens were detected using real-time PCR for broad-spectrum screening of respiratory viruses. Results: Viral etiology was established in approximately 50% of cases. The most frequently detected pathogen was Human rhinovirus (HRV) (35.6%), followed by Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and Human adenovirus (HAdV). Despite its predominance, HRV did not demonstrate nosological specificity. The strongest associations with lower respiratory tract infections were identified for RSV (OR = 3.2) and Human bocavirus (HBoV; OR = 2.4), predominantly within the pneumonia category. RSV was also associated with bronchitis/bronchiolitis (OR = 1.8). Significant associations with upper respiratory tract infections were established for Influenza viruses (OR = 10.4) and HAdV, including nasopharyngitis (OR = 3.88) and acute tonsillitis (OR = 3.9). HAdV additionally demonstrated an association with otitis media (OR = 5.1). Severe disease was registered in 52.3% of all clinical observations and occurred most frequently among young children, particularly in cases associated with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV >80%), as well as with human bocavirus (HBoV) and Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) (~55–59%). Co-infections were not associated with increased disease severity compared with monoinfections (OR = 1.1). Conclusions: The obtained results highlight the contribution of specific etiological agents to severe respiratory infections in children. These findings support the prioritization of such pathogens in clinical diagnostics, including the design of diagnostic algorithms and the selection of patient management strategies in pediatric populations.

papers.title_zh: 儿童急性呼吸道感染的病因及临床表现:俄罗斯莫斯科的回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Acute respiratory viral infections (ARVIs) are the leading cause of pediatric morbidity and exhibit considerable clinical heterogeneity. The analysis of clinical and etiological associations, as well as the identification of factors linked to severe ARVI cases, is essential for effective epidemiological surveillance. Methods: A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted including 1362 non-COVID-19 pediatric cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs), registered between 2021 and 2024. Viral pathogens were detected using real-time PCR for broad-spectrum screening of respiratory viruses. Results: Viral etiology was established in approximately 50% of cases. The most frequently detected pathogen was Human rhinovirus (HRV) (35.6%), followed by Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and Human adenovirus (HAdV). Despite its predominance, HRV did not demonstrate nosological specificity. The strongest associations with lower respiratory tract infections were identified for RSV (OR = 3.2) and Human bocavirus (HBoV; OR = 2.4), predominantly within the pneumonia category. RSV was also associated with bronchitis/bronchiolitis (OR = 1.8). Significant associations with upper respiratory tract infections were established for Influenza viruses (OR = 10.4) and HAdV, including nasopharyngitis (OR = 3.88) and acute tonsillitis (OR = 3.9). HAdV additionally demonstrated an association with otitis media (OR = 5.1). Severe disease was registered in 52.3% of all clinical observations and occurred most frequently among young children, particularly in cases associated with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV >80%), as well as with human bocavirus (HBoV) and Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) (~55–59%). Co-infections were not associated with increased disease severity compared with monoinfections (OR = 1.1). Conclusions: The obtained results highlight the contribution of specific etiological agents to severe respiratory infections in children. These findings support the prioritization of such pathogens in clinical diagnostics, including the design of diagnostic algorithms and the selection of patient management strategies in pediatric populations.

papers.title: Association between nirsevimab coverage and pediatric emergency department visits for bronchiolitis in 12 European countries: An interrupted time-series analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nirsevimab was introduced to prevent Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infants. Despite its proven effectiveness and similar guidelines across Europe, bronchiolitis reduction varied across Europe. This study explored whether nirsevimab coverage among targeted populations (born in- and out-of-season) was associated to this variability. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We used routinely collected data from 27 pediatric emergency departments across 12 European countries (01/2018-03/2024). All bronchiolitis cases aged <12 months were included. Regions were classified as intervention or control based on nirsevimab implementation. Coverage was obtained from official regional reports. We estimated changes in monthly case using controlled interrupted time-series models accounting for seasonality and temporal trends, by age-groups (0-3 and 3-12 months) and regions during the intervention period (10/2023-03/2024) and examined their correlation to coverage using Pearson's test. Urinary tract infections served as a control outcome. We included 107,088 bronchiolitis cases. Reductions varied widely across regions and age-groups, from +0.6% (95% CI [-9.4, +20.5]) to -61.0% (95% CI [-67.8, -35.2]). Coverage strongly correlated with bronchiolitis reduction across age-groups and regions (ρ = -0.86, p = 0.001). Bronchiolitis trends in control countries remained stable, as did urinary tract infections. As an ecological study, causality cannot be inferred and unmeasured regional differences may have contributed to the variability. CONCLUSIONS: This multinational interrupted time-series analysis identified coverage as a key factor associated to bronchiolitis reduction across age-groups and European regions. Implementation choices across Europe likely influenced coverage, highlighting that nirsevimab benefits depend not only on its intrinsic efficacy, but also on how effectively it is delivered.
authors: Victoria Trenchs Sáinz de la Maza

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between nirsevimab coverage and reductions in pediatric emergency department visits for RSV bronchiolitis across 12 European countries using an interrupted time-series analysis. The research aimed to understand why bronchiolitis reduction varied despite similar guidelines and proven effectiveness of nirsevimab. The study included 107,088 bronchiolitis cases aged <12 months from 27 emergency departments between 2018 and 2024. Using controlled interrupted time-series models, the authors found that bronchiolitis reductions varied widely across regions and age-groups, with coverage strongly correlated with reductions (ρ = -0.86, p = 0.001). The results suggest that the effectiveness of nirsevimab depends on its coverage and delivery, which has implications for public health strategies. However, the study's ecological design limits the ability to infer causality, and unmeasured regional differences may have influenced the outcomes, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:引入 尼塞韦单抗 是为了预防婴儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 毛细支气管炎。尽管 毛细支气管炎 的有效性已得到证实,并且在整个欧洲都有类似的指导方针,但欧洲各地的 毛细支气管炎 减少量各不相同。本研究探讨了目标人群(出生在季节内和反季节)中的 尼塞韦单抗 覆盖率是否与这种变异性相关。方法和结果:我们使用了从 12 个欧洲国家的 27 个儿科急诊科常规收集的数据 (01/2018-03/2024)。所有年龄<12个月的毛细支气管炎病例均被纳入。根据 尼塞韦单抗 的实施情况,将区域划分为干预或控制。报道来自官方区域报告。我们使用考虑了季节性和时间趋势的受控中断时间序列模型,按干预期间(10/2023-03/2024)的年龄组(0-3 个月和 3-12 个月)和地区估计了每月病例的变化,并使用 Pearson 检验检查了它们与覆盖率的相关性。尿路感染作为对照结果。我们纳入了 107,088 个 毛细支气管炎 案例。不同地区和年龄组的下降幅度差异很大,从 +0.6% (95% CI [-9.4,+20.5]) 到 -61.0% (95% CI [-67.8,-35.2])。各年龄组和地区的覆盖率与 毛细支气管炎 减少密切相关(ρ = -0.86,p = 0.001)。对照国家的 毛细支气管炎 趋势保持稳定,尿路感染也是如此。作为一项生态研究,因果关系无法推断,无法测量的区域差异可能导致了变异性。结论:这项跨国间断时间序列分析确定,覆盖范围是与各年龄组和欧洲地区 毛细支气管炎 减少相关的关键因素。欧洲各地的实施选择可能会影响覆盖范围,这凸显出 尼塞韦单抗 的好处不仅取决于其内在功效,还取决于其交付的效率。

papers.title: Changes in Lung Sounds During the Acute Stage of RSV Acute Bronchiolitis in Infants.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Changes in the respiratory function over time in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced acute bronchiolitis were evaluated by a lung sound analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively examined changes in lung sound parameters over time in 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis. We evaluated the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds using a conventional method and analyzed the frequency characteristics of inspiratory sounds using new automated analysis software program. We examined changes in these lung sound parameters over time during and after hospitalization and compared these data with those of age-matched healthy children. RESULTS: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after the onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after the onset of RSV acute bronchiolitis. Some lung sound parameters in patients with RSV acute bronchiolitis did not return to normal even by 14 days after the onset. CONCLUSIONS: This finding is considered a characteristic of RSV acute bronchiolitis in infants and is meaningful in terms of post-treatment management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate changes in respiratory function over time in RSV-induced acute bronchiolitis, addressing the need to understand the progression of lung sounds in infants with this condition.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study was conducted on 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis, examining lung sound parameters during and after hospitalization.
analysis.methods: Lung sound parameters were analyzed using both conventional methods and new automated software, with comparisons made to age-matched healthy children's data.
analysis.main_results: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after onset. Some parameters did not return to normal even by 14 days post-onset.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the dynamic nature of lung sounds in RSV acute bronchiolitis, suggesting that certain parameters may persist beyond the initial recovery phase, which is novel in the context of respiratory sound analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the monitoring of respiratory function in infants with RSV bronchiolitis, potentially informing post-treatment management and the timing of clinical assessments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis and the generalizability of findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated changes in lung sounds during the acute stage of RSV-induced bronchiolitis in infants. By analyzing 138 lung sound samples from 54 children, it found that the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds peaked within 4 days after onset and improved over time. However, significant changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed between 5 to 10 days post-onset, and some parameters remained abnormal even by 14 days. The authors interpret these findings as characteristic of RSV bronchiolitis, suggesting their relevance for post-treatment monitoring. The study's retrospective design and reliance on abstract-only evidence limit its depth and generalizability, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)引起的急性毛细支气管炎中呼吸功能随时间的变化,以了解该条件下婴儿肺部声音进展的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 54 名诊断为急性 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的儿童(中位年龄为 7 个月)进行了一项回顾性研究,检查了住院期间和住院后的肺音参数。
elements_zh.methods: 使用传统方法和新的自动化软件分析肺部声音参数,并与年龄匹配的健康儿童的数据进行比较。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为监测 RSV 毛细支气管炎 婴儿的呼吸功能提供了见解,可能为 治疗 后的管理和临床评估的时间安排提供信息。

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:通过肺音分析评估 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 诱导的急性 毛细支气管炎 呼吸功能随时间的变化。方法:我们回顾性检查了 54 名诊断为急性 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的儿童(中位年龄为 7 个月)肺音参数随时间的变化。我们使用传统方法评估吸气和呼气声音的功率,并使用新的自动分析软件程序分析吸气声音的频率特性。我们检查了住院期间和住院后这些肺音参数随时间的变化,并将这些数据与年龄匹配的健康儿童的数据进行了比较。结果:在 54 名婴儿的 138 个肺音样本中,吸气音和呼气音的力量在发病后 4 天内最强,并随着时间的推移而改善。相比之下,RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 发病后 5 至 10 天观察到吸气音参数的最大变化。RSV急性毛细支气管炎患者的一些肺音参数即使在发病后14天也没有恢复正常。结论:这一发现被认为是婴儿 RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 的一个特征,对于 毛细支气管炎 后的管理具有重要意义。

papers.title: Diversification without convergence: national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra diverge as they diversify, 1990–2023
papers.abstract: BackgroundNational childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying nearly everywhere -- within-country diversity rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 -- yet whether countries are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths is unknown. We quantified between-country compositional distance of national pathogen spectra over the same period. MethodsWe built national pathogen share vectors from Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions (26 pathogens, 204 countries, ages 0-19 years) at five timepoints spanning 1990-2023. Between-country distance was measured as all pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD; primary) and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with Baselga and Jaccard decompositions; robustness was assessed across metrics, pathogen panels, low-count thresholds and a balanced panel of 107 countries. ResultsMean pairwise JSD rose from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity rose +120% and the balanced panel +423%. Divergence was entirely balanced variation (share reallocation), with spectrum richness rising from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. Dispersion rose fastest for influenza (coefficient of variation 0.03 to 0.55) and respiratory syncytial virus (0.08 to 0.48). Within-region distance rose in every computable GBD super-region (five of seven): divergence occurs within regions, not between blocs. ConclusionsNational spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes as vaccine-preventable dominance recedes at different speeds. Diversification is universal, but convergence is absent: the transition at the etiologic-spectrum level is asynchronous and path-dependent, with implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance. Summary boxO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSO_LIEpidemiological transition theory and the global health convergence agenda imply that national cause-of-death structures become more alike as mortality declines, but this expectation has been tested mainly at the level of mortality rates and broad cause groups, not etiologic spectra. C_LIO_LIWithin-country (alpha) diversity of the childhood respiratory pathogen spectrum rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023. C_LI What this study addsO_LIBetween-country (beta) compositional distance roughly tripled over the same period (mean pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergence +238%, 1990 to 2023), robust to distance metric, pathogen panel, COVID-19 exclusion, low-count threshold, and a fixed balanced panel. C_LIO_LIDivergence is driven entirely by reallocation of pathogen shares (balanced variation), is fastest for viral pathogens, and occurs within every GBD super-region, indicating that countries diversify along country-specific paths rather than toward a common spectrum.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景几乎所有国家的儿童呼吸道病原体谱系都在多样化——1990年至2023年间,204个国家中有203个国家的国内多样性有所增加——但各国是朝着共同谱系多样化还是沿着不同路径多样化尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 方法我们根据 2023 年全球疾病负担研究下呼吸道感染病因学归因(26 个病原体,204 个国家,年龄 0-19 岁)在 1990 年至 2023 年的五个时间点建立了国家病原体共享 媒介。
elements_zh.methods: 国家间距离通过所有成对的 Jensen-Shannon 散度(JSD;主要)和 Bray-Curtis 差异进行测量,并采用 Baselga 和 Jaccard 分解;稳健性通过指标、病原体小组、低计数阈值和 107 个国家的平衡小组进行了评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 分歧是完全平衡的变异(份额重新分配),26 种病原体的谱丰富度从 18.5 上升到 21.1。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: C_LIO_LI 1990 年至 2023 年间,204 个国家中的 203 个国家的儿童呼吸道病原体谱系的国内 (alpha) 多样性有所上升。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 多样化是普遍的,但缺乏趋同性:病因谱水平的转变是异步的和路径依赖的,对经验性的 治疗 政策和病原体 监测 具有影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: C_LI 这项研究增加了什么O_LI国家之间(β)组成距离在同一时期大致增加了两倍(1990 年至 2023 年平均成对 Jensen-Shannon 散度 +238%),对距离度量、病原体组、COVID-19 排除、低计数阈值和固定平衡组具有鲁棒性。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景几乎所有国家的儿童呼吸道病原体谱系都在多样化——1990年至2023年间,204个国家中有203个国家的国内多样性有所增加——但各国是朝着共同谱系多样化还是沿着不同路径多样化尚不清楚。我们量化了同一时期国家病原体谱的国家间组成距离。方法我们根据 2023 年全球疾病负担研究下呼吸道感染病因学归因(26 个病原体,204 个国家,年龄 0-19 岁)在 1990 年至 2023 年的五个时间点建立了国家病原体共享 媒介。国家间距离通过所有成对的 Jensen-Shannon 散度(JSD;主要)和 Bray-Curtis 差异进行测量,并采用 Baselga 和 Jaccard 分解;稳健性通过指标、病原体小组、低计数阈值和 107 个国家的平衡小组进行了评估。结果平均成对 JSD 从 1990 年的 0.0084 升至 2023 年的 0.0283(+238%;趋势 p = 0.030),于 2021 年达到峰值(+283%),并于 2023 年部分回落。Bray-Curtis 差异增加了 +120%,平衡面板增加了 +423%。分歧是完全平衡的变异(份额重新分配),26 种病原体的谱丰富度从 18.5 上升到 21.1。流感(变异系数 0.03 至 0.55)和 呼吸道合胞病毒(变异系数 0.08 至 0.48)的离散度上升最快。每个可计算的 GBD 超级区域(七个中的五个)的区域内距离都增加了:分歧发生在区域内部,而不是集团之间。结论 随着 疫苗 可预防的主导地位以不同的速度消退,国家频谱正在沿着国家特定轴重新排序。多样化是普遍的,但缺乏趋同性:病因谱水平的转变是异步的和路径依赖的,对经验性的 治疗 政策和病原体 监测 具有影响。摘要框O_ST_ABS 关于此主题的已知信息C_ST_ABSO_L流行病学转变理论和全球健康趋同议程意味着,随着 死亡率 下降,国家死因结构变得更加相似,但这种预期主要在 死亡率 比率和广泛原因组(而非病因谱)水平上进行了检验。C_LIO_LI 1990 年至 2023 年间,204 个国家中的 203 个国家的儿童呼吸道病原体谱系的国内 (alpha) 多样性有所上升。C_LI 这项研究增加了什么O_LI国家之间(β)组成距离在同一时期大致增加了两倍(1990 年至 2023 年平均成对 Jensen-Shannon 散度 +238%),对距离度量、病原体组、COVID-19 排除、低计数阈值和固定平衡组具有鲁棒性。C_LIO_LIDivergence 完全由病原体份额的重新分配(平衡变异)驱动,对于病毒病原体来说速度最快,并且发生在每个 GBD 大区域内,表明各国沿着特定国家的路径而不是朝着共同的谱系多样化。

papers.title: Forecasting viral evolution from phylogenetic trees
papers.abstract: Viral mutation forecasting plays a key role in pandemic preparedness by enabling researchers to anticipate novel variants and design proactive interventions. Evolutionary histories, represented as phylogenetic trees, offer key insights into the emergence of past and present strains, yet their role in predicting future sequence changes remains largely unexplored. We introduce antiGen, a machine learning model that forecasts the evolutionary future of viruses by learning from their evolutionary past. antiGen achieves state-of-the-art performance for predicting mutations to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, anticipating never-before-seen mutations and mutations that emerge years after the model's training window. antiGen-forecasted spike mutations also retain pseudoviral infectivity in vitro. Moreover, antiGen demonstrates leading predictive performance on surface proteins of influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and dengue virus despite far less available sequencing data. Viral evolution models that explicitly learn from phylogenetic structure offer a valuable resource for applications ranging from epidemiological modeling to therapeutic development.
